checkpoint_plan.resume_instruction: Reuse this unchanged run card with --resume <completed checkpoint directory>.
checkpoint_plan.selection: lowest validation loss; earlier step wins equal loss

comparison_plan: Keep both exports. Measure unweighted token loss and first-token Yes/No performance on the same train/validation rows; run oracle generation on all48 validation examples and matched full v3 validation with the fixed scope policy. Retain all failures and abstentions. Weighted loss is not directly comparable with initial uniform loss.
estimate_assumptions: Conditional planning estimate from three steady optimizer samples and two full validation/checkpoint writes at this exact pilot shape; 2x time buffer and 25% reserved-memory margin rounded up to0.25GiB. Same GPU/software and data assumed; thermal throttling, OneDrive/disk variation and competing processes remain uncertain. Not a runtime or memory guarantee.
finite_stopping_condition: Exactly 240 optimizer steps (five passes); no automatic retry, extension or final-test tuning.
initialization: Same pinned pretrained FLAN-T5-small, seed, data, targets, optimizer, learning rate, token shape and finite cap as initial run; only the comparison decision-token objective changes.
limitations: Automated development review is disclosed and cannot establish independent human label quality.
Only six entity families and twelve shared question forms; no final-test or unrestricted-language claim.
No early accuracy guarantee. Stop at the fixed cap; evaluate validation and document failures before any targeted revision.

loss_objective.rule: first target token of reviewed comparison yes/no rows has weight 8; other valid tokens 1; padding 0

question: Does giving the opening Yes/No token equal extra weight for both comparison classes improve generated comparison polarity on the unchanged held-out edits, while preserving complete factual answers?
